gloss_en: The illuminating speech (dibbur ha-me'ir) — speech/utterance that shines with light, attained only by making God's honor complete through humility and self-abasement (one's own honor as nothing), which then illuminates the way to repentance and to the depths of Torah understanding (Likutey Moharan I:11); identified with the 'tzipparta' (bird) of the Zohar; covers singular (דבור המאיר) and plural (דבורים המאירים) forms and the periphrasis 'the speech that will illuminate for him' (דבור שיאיר לו)
